# Abstract

Forest managers using retention forestry need information on regeneration and
fuel development to design productive stands in fire-adapted ecosystems. We
analyzed 10-year remeasurement data from the Redwood Multiaged Experiment in
Jackson Demonstration State Forest, California. The experiment compared group
selection, aggregated retention, and low- and high-density dispersed retention
treatments and measured regeneration, sprout growth, and surface fuel loading.

Redwood regeneration responded strongly to increasing canopy openness, whereas
tanoak responses were more modest. Sprout-height findings will remain part of
the main regeneration evidence. Fuel measurements describe conditions before
and after precommercial thinning, including the PCT-associated contrast. The
manuscript will evaluate how overstory retention affects regeneration while
presenting fuel components in a form useful for integrated silviculture, fuels,
and fire management.
